items.title: Radiology fires back at report claiming providers ‘gaming’ No Surprises Act - Radiology Business
items.reason: The article addresses provider behavior and compliance interpretation under the No Surprises Act, which directly relates to implementation issues and enforcement concerns that affect revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: Radiology providers are responding to allegations that the specialty is manipulating the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process to achieve favorable payment outcomes. The report suggests some radiology groups are strategically using the IDR mechanism in ways that may circumvent the Act's intended balance-billing protections, prompting the radiology community to defend their practices. This development is significant for revenue-cycle teams because it highlights disputes over proper implementation and interpretation of No Surprises Act rules, which could influence how IDR claims are evaluated and what constitutes compliant behavior under the federal law.

items.title: Bill proposes ‘sensible guardrails’ to stop AI-driven Medicare Advantage denials - McKnight's Long-Term Care News
items.reason: This item addresses proposed regulatory action to restrict Medicare Advantage payer denials (specifically AI-driven denials), which falls directly under CMS/Medicare Advantage enforcement and payer policies that affect revenue cycle operations.
items.summary: A bill has been introduced proposing regulatory guardrails to restrict AI-driven claim denials by Medicare Advantage plans. The legislation aims to impose what sponsors describe as 'sensible' limitations on automated denial systems used by payers, addressing concerns that AI-driven denials are inappropriately rejecting claims without adequate clinical justification. This regulatory proposal directly impacts Medicare Advantage insurers' claims-processing practices and would affect how revenue-cycle teams handle denial appeals and claim submissions to MA plans. The measure signals legislative intent to constrain payer enforcement of denials through automated systems, which has significant implications for provider cash flow and claims management workflows.

items.title: CMS releases 2025 report on program audits, enforcement for Medicare Advantage, Part D - American Hospital Association
items.reason: CMS enforcement and audit reports on Medicare Advantage and Part D payers are directly relevant to payer enforcement and regulatory actions that impact revenue-cycle operations and reimbursement.
items.summary: CMS released its 2025 report on program audits and enforcement activities targeting Medicare Advantage and Part D plans. The report details regulatory oversight, audit findings, and enforcement actions taken against payers operating these federal programs, which directly affect how payers process claims and manage provider networks. Revenue-cycle teams need visibility into CMS enforcement trends and sanctioned payer behaviors, as these actions often result in payment corrections, network adjustments, and changes to claims-handling procedures that impact provider reimbursement workflows.
